1	"""Pydantic models for all persisted records, plus the canonical JSON writer.
2	
3	Every artifact on disk is produced through :func:`canonical_dumps` so that two
4	builds with the same seed and provider are byte-for-byte identical.
5	
6	Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — the post lists what a
7	    shard actually holds: "Bloom Filters: used to quickly check if phrases exist",
8	    "Each shard has a trained Zstandard text compression dictionary", and
9	    "Vocabulary: the set of unique words in this shard" (shard 11,343 is quoted at a
10	    vocabulary of 64,992 terms). :class:`ShardManifest` had none of those three, so
11	    they are added here as first-class manifest fields. Local copy:
12	    ``docs/blog-archive/the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md``
13	
14	Assumptions: the post does not say how the three artifacts are serialised, so the
15	    two binary ones travel base64 inside JSON — the bloom bit array as the payload
16	    produced by :meth:`cybernaut_mini.shard_artifacts.PhraseBloom.to_payload`, the
17	    zstd dictionary as a bare base64 string. All three fields default to ``None``
18	    because a shard too small to train a dictionary on is legitimate (the tail of a
19	    k-means split) and because a manifest held in memory usually does *not* carry
20	    them: :class:`~cybernaut_mini.indexing.LoadedIndex` deliberately leaves them
21	    unpopulated and fetches them per shard on demand, since 1,000 resident
22	    vocabularies of 65,536 terms is gigabytes of heap.
23	
24	Alternatives rejected: a single ``artifacts`` sub-model holding all three. Rejected
25	    because the three have genuinely different lifetimes — the bloom is ~1.2 KB and
26	    cheap to keep, the vocabulary is the one that cannot be held 1,000 times over —
27	    and one field would force an all-or-nothing load. Also rejected: validating
28	    ``artifact_version`` inside the models. A model that refuses to parse an old
29	    record cannot produce the error message that tells the user which version they
30	    have; that check belongs at the index boundary, in
31	    :meth:`~cybernaut_mini.indexing.LoadedIndex.load`.
32	"""
33	
34	from __future__ import annotations
35	
36	import json
37	import math
38	from datetime import datetime
39	from typing import Any
40	
41	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator
42	
43	#: Bumped to "2" when shards gained their bloom filter, zstd dictionary and
44	#: vocabulary, and the index layout gained per-shard artifact sidecars and
45	#: JSONL offset sidecars. A "1" index has none of those files, so it is rejected
46	#: at load rather than read as a shard set with three permanently-absent
47	#: artifacts — see :meth:`cybernaut_mini.indexing.LoadedIndex.load`.
48	ARTIFACT_VERSION = "2"
49	
50	FLOAT_DECIMALS = 8
51	
52	
53	def _round_floats(value: Any) -> Any:
54	    if isinstance(value, float):
55	        if not math.isfinite(value):
56	            msg = f"non-finite float in artifact: {value!r}"
57	            raise ValueError(msg)
58	        rounded = round(value, FLOAT_DECIMALS)
59	        return 0.0 if rounded == 0 else rounded
60	    if isinstance(value, dict):
61	        return {key: _round_floats(item) for key, item in value.items()}
62	    if isinstance(value, list):
63	        return [_round_floats(item) for item in value]
64	    return value
65	
66	
67	def canonical_dumps(obj: Any) -> str:
68	    """Serialize to deterministic JSON: sorted keys, compact, floats at 8 decimals."""
69	    return json.dumps(_round_floats(obj), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
70	
71	
72	def model_canonical_dumps(model: BaseModel) -> str:
73	    return canonical_dumps(model.model_dump(mode="json"))
74	
75	
76	class Document(BaseModel):
77	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
78	
79	    id: str = Field(min_length=1)
80	    title: str
81	    text: str
82	    url: str | None = None
83	    language: str | None = None
84	    published_at: datetime | None = None
85	    metadata: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
86	
87	    @field_validator("title", "text")
88	    @classmethod
89	    def _non_empty(cls, value: str) -> str:
90	        if not value.strip():
91	            msg = "must be non-empty"
92	            raise ValueError(msg)
93	        return value
94	
95	
96	class MetadataFilter(BaseModel):
97	    """Typed metadata filter; fields combine with logical AND.
98	
99	    ``extra="forbid"`` makes any unsupported operator a validation error.
100	    """
101	
102	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
103	
104	    language: list[str] | None = None
105	    published_from: datetime | None = None
106	    published_to: datetime | None = None
107	    metadata_equals: dict[str, Any] | None = None
108	
109	    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
110	        return (
111	            self.language is None
112	            and self.published_from is None
113	            and self.published_to is None
114	            and self.metadata_equals is None
115	        )
116	
117	    def matches(self, document: Document) -> bool:
118	        if self.language is not None and document.language not in self.language:
119	            return False
120	        if self.published_from is not None and (
121	            document.published_at is None or document.published_at < self.published_from
122	        ):
123	            return False
124	        if self.published_to is not None and (
125	            document.published_at is None or document.published_at >= self.published_to
126	        ):
127	            return False
128	        if self.metadata_equals is not None:
129	            for key, expected in self.metadata_equals.items():
130	                if document.metadata.get(key) != expected:
131	                    return False
132	        return True
133	
134	
135	class ShardKeyword(BaseModel):
136	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
137	
138	    term: str
139	    weight: float
140	
141	
142	class ShardEntity(BaseModel):
143	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
144	
145	    text: str
146	    count: int
147	
148	
149	class ShardManifest(BaseModel):
150	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
151	
152	    shard_id: int
153	    document_ids: list[str]
154	    centroid: list[float]
155	    title: str
156	    summary: str
157	    keywords: list[ShardKeyword]
158	    entities: list[ShardEntity]
159	    term_graph: dict[str, dict[str, float]]
160	    document_count: int
161	    artifact_version: str = ARTIFACT_VERSION
162	    embedding_model: str
163	
164	    #: Bloom filter over this shard's important phrases, as produced by
165	    #: :meth:`cybernaut_mini.shard_artifacts.PhraseBloom.to_payload` (the bit array
166	    #: is base64 inside it). ``None`` means "not loaded / not built", never "empty":
167	    #: an empty shard still gets a real, always-false filter.
168	    phrase_bloom: dict[str, Any] | None = None
169	    #: Base64 of this shard's trained Zstandard dictionary. ``None`` when zstd
170	    #: refused to train — a shard of a handful of short documents does not contain
171	    #: enough repeated material — in which case
172	    #: :func:`cybernaut_mini.shard_artifacts.compression_score` scores it 0.0.
173	    zstd_dictionary: str | None = None
174	    #: This shard's unique terms, as produced by
175	    #: :meth:`cybernaut_mini.shard_artifacts.Vocabulary.to_payload`. The single
176	    #: largest field a manifest can carry, which is why it is loaded per shard on
177	    #: demand rather than with the manifest.
178	    vocabulary: dict[str, Any] | None = None
179	
180	    def without_artifacts(self) -> ShardManifest:
181	        """A copy with the three artifact fields cleared.
182	
183	        This is the form the manifest takes on disk and in memory: the payloads live
184	        in a per-shard sidecar so that loading 1,000 manifests stays cheap.
185	        """
186	        return self.model_copy(
187	            update={"phrase_bloom": None, "zstd_dictionary": None, "vocabulary": None}
188	        )
189	
190	    def has_artifacts(self) -> bool:
191	        """True when all three artifact fields are populated on this instance."""
192	        return self.phrase_bloom is not None and self.vocabulary is not None
193	
194	    @field_validator("document_ids")
195	    @classmethod
196	    def _non_empty_shard(cls, value: list[str]) -> list[str]:
197	        if not value:
198	            msg = "shard must contain at least one document"
199	            raise ValueError(msg)
200	        return value
201	
202	
203	class IndexMeta(BaseModel):
204	    """Top-level index metadata; presence of the `_VALID` marker refers to this record."""
205	
206	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
207	
208	    artifact_version: str = ARTIFACT_VERSION
209	    embedding_model: str
210	    #: Weights revision used at build time. Queries must embed with the same
211	    #: revision or their vectors are not comparable to the stored ones.
212	    #: None means the build did not pin one (indexes written before this field
213	    #: existed also load as None).
214	    embedding_revision: str | None = None
215	    embedding_dim: int
216	    n_shards: int
217	    n_documents: int
218	    seed: int
219	
220	
221	class SearchHit(BaseModel):
222	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
223	
224	    document: Document
225	    rank: int
226	    score: float
227	    shard_id: int
228	    bm25_score: float | None = None
229	    bm25_rank: int | None = None
230	    dense_score: float | None = None
231	    dense_rank: int | None = None
232	    rrf_contributions: dict[str, float] = Field(default_factory=dict)
233	    query_variant: str
234	    expansion_terms: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
235	    snippet: str = Field(max_length=500)
236	
237

239	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
240	
241	    relevance: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
242	    coverage: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
243	    redundancy: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
244	    reason: str = Field(max_length=240)
245	
246	
247	class QueryCandidate(BaseModel):
248	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

252	    expansions: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

1	"""Custom Kedro datasets for the artifact formats used by this project.
2	
3	All JSON-bearing datasets serialize through :func:`cybernaut_mini.models.canonical_dumps`
4	so pipeline outputs keep the byte-for-byte determinism guarantee.
5	
6	Every path the corpus and the index travel goes through a dataset in this module,
7	so the catalog — not a node body — owns all file and network I/O. That is what makes
8	``kedro-viz`` show real lineage and what lets ``conf/prod`` swap a local corpus for a
9	Hugging Face one without touching pipeline code.
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import os
15	from pathlib import Path
16	from typing import Any
17	
18	import numpy as np
19	import numpy.typing as npt
20	from kedro.io import AbstractDataset
21	from kedro.io.core import DatasetError
22	
23	from cybernaut_mini.models import canonical_dumps
24	
25	#: Committed fixture directories. A pipeline writing here would silently rewrite the
26	#: golden corpus that the determinism tests compare against, so saves are refused.
27	#: Reads are unaffected — `--input data/sample/documents.jsonl` stays supported.
28	PROTECTED_DIRS = ("data/sample", "data/00_reference")
29	
30	
31	def _guard_protected(filepath: Path) -> None:
32	    """Refuse to write over a committed fixture."""
33	    try:
34	        relative = filepath.resolve().relative_to(Path.cwd().resolve())
35	    except ValueError:
36	        # Outside the project (e.g. a pytest tmp_path); nothing to protect.
37	        return
38	    as_posix = relative.as_posix()
39	    for protected in PROTECTED_DIRS:
40	        if as_posix == protected or as_posix.startswith(f"{protected}/"):
41	            msg = (
42	                f"refusing to write {as_posix}: {protected} holds committed fixtures. "
43	                f"Point this catalog entry at a generated layer "
44	                f"(data/01_raw, data/02_intermediate, data/03_primary) instead."
45	            )
46	            raise DatasetError(msg)
47	
48	
49	class CanonicalJsonDataset(AbstractDataset[Any, Any]):
50	    """A single JSON value written with the canonical writer."""
51	
52	    def __init__(self, filepath: str) -> None:
53	        self._filepath = Path(filepath)
54

137	class HuggingFaceDataset(AbstractDataset[None, list[dict[str, Any]]]):
138	    """Read-only corpus source backed by a Hugging Face Hub dataset repo.
139	
140	    ``revision`` is **required and must be a commit SHA or tag**, never a branch
141	    name: a production shard is only reproducible if the corpus it was built from
142	    is pinned. ``main`` is rejected outright.
143	
144	    Requires the ``hf`` extra (``uv sync --extra hf``). The import is deferred to
145	    :meth:`load` so the core package — and the whole offline test suite — never
146	    depends on it.
147	    """
148	
149	    #: Refs that move over time and so cannot pin a reproducible build.
150	    _MUTABLE_REFS = frozenset({"main", "master", "head", "refs/heads/main"})
151	
152	    #: Shipped in conf/prod as a deliberate tripwire — a real SHA must replace it.
153	    _PLACEHOLDER_REF = "replace_with_commit_sha"
154	
155	    def __init__(
156	        self,
157	        repo_id: str,
158	        revision: str,
159	        split: str = "train",
160	        columns: list[str] | None = None,
161	        max_rows: int | None = None,
162	        token_env: str = "HF_TOKEN",
163	    ) -> None:
164	        normalized_ref = (revision or "").strip().lower()
165	        if normalized_ref == self._PLACEHOLDER_REF:
166	            msg = (
167	                f"HuggingFaceDataset({repo_id!r}): revision is still the placeholder. "
168	                f"Resolve the real SHA and paste it into conf/prod/catalog.yml:\n"
169	                f"  uv run python -c \"from huggingface_hub import HfApi; "
170	                f"print(HfApi().dataset_info('{repo_id}').sha)\""
171	            )
172	            raise DatasetError(msg)
173	        if not normalized_ref or normalized_ref in self._MUTABLE_REFS:
174	            msg = (
175	                f"HuggingFaceDataset({repo_id!r}): revision must pin an immutable "
176	                f"commit SHA or tag, got {revision!r}. A moving ref makes the built "
177	                f"index unreproducible."
178	            )
179	            raise DatasetError(msg)
180	        self._repo_id = repo_id
181	        self._revision = revision
182	        self._split = split
183	        self._columns = columns
184	        self._max_rows = max_rows
185	        self._token_env = token_env
186	
187	    def load(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
188	        try:
189	            # The Hugging Face `datasets` package, not this module: Python 3 has no
190	            # implicit relative imports, so the absolute name wins despite the clash.
191	            from datasets import load_dataset
192	        except ImportError as exc:
193	            msg = (
194	                "HuggingFaceDataset needs the 'hf' extra; install it with "
195	                "`uv sync --extra hf`"
196	            )
197	            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc
198	
199	        # A private repo needs a token; a public one must still work without it.
200	        token = os.environ.get(self._token_env) or None
201	
202	        split = self._split
203	        if self._max_rows is not None:
204	            # Slice in the split spec so only the requested rows are materialised.
205	            split = f"{split}[:{self._max_rows}]"
206	
207	        dataset = load_dataset(
208	            self._repo_id,
209	            revision=self._revision,
210	            split=split,
211	            token=token,
212	        )
213	        if self._columns is not None:
214	            missing = set(self._columns) - set(dataset.column_names)
215	            if missing:
216	                msg = (
217	                    f"HuggingFaceDataset({self._repo_id!r}): requested columns "
218	                    f"{sorted(missing)} are absent; available: {sorted(dataset.column_names)}"
219	                )
220	                raise DatasetError(msg)
221	            dataset = dataset.select_columns(self._columns)
222	
223	        rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = [dict(row) for row in dataset]
224	        return rows
225	
226	    def save(self, data: None) -> None:
227	        msg = (
228	            f"HuggingFaceDataset({self._repo_id!r}) is read-only; write the "
229	            f"normalised corpus to a JsonlDataset in data/01_raw instead."
230	        )
231	        raise DatasetError(msg)
232	
233	    def _exists(self) -> bool:
234	        # Existence would require a network round-trip; report False so Kedro
235	        # never treats a Hub lookup as a cheap local check.
236	        return False
237	
238	    def _describe(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
239	        return {
240	            "repo_id": self._repo_id,
241	            "revision": self._revision,
242	            "split": self._split,
243	            "columns": self._columns,
244	            "max_rows": self._max_rows,
245	        }

248	class ShardIndexDataset(AbstractDataset[dict[str, Any], Any]):
249	    """The built shard index directory, as a single catalog-addressable artifact.
250	
251	    ``save`` accepts the plain-dict payload emitted by the ``build_index`` node and
252	    performs the canonical write; ``load`` returns a query-ready
253	    :class:`~cybernaut_mini.indexing.LoadedIndex`. Keeping the conversion here means
254	    nodes stay pure functions over plain data and never touch the filesystem.
255	    """
256	
257	    def __init__(self, filepath: str) -> None:
258	        self._filepath = Path(filepath)
259	
260	    def load(self) -> Any:
261	        from cybernaut_mini.indexing import LoadedIndex
262	
263	        return LoadedIndex.load(self._filepath)

265	    def save(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
266	        from cybernaut_mini.indexing import write_index
267	        from cybernaut_mini.models import Document, IndexMeta, ShardManifest
268	
269	        try:
270	            meta = IndexMeta.model_validate(data["meta"])
271	            documents = [Document.model_validate(d) for d in data["documents"]]
272	            manifests = [ShardManifest.model_validate(m) for m in data["manifests"]]
273	            vectors = np.array(data["vectors"], dtype=np.float32)
274	            doc_tokens: dict[str, list[str]] = data["doc_tokens"]
275	        except KeyError as exc:
276	            msg = f"ShardIndexDataset payload is missing key {exc}"
277	            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc
278	
279	        write_index(
280	            self._filepath,
281	            meta=meta,
282	            documents=documents,
283	            vectors=vectors,
284	            manifests=manifests,
285	            doc_tokens=doc_tokens,
286	        )
287	
288	    def _exists(self) -> bool:
289	        # `_VALID` is written last, so its presence is the completeness signal.
290	        return (self._filepath / "_VALID").exists()
291	
292	    def _describe(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
293	        return {"filepath": str(self._filepath)}

1	"""Normalisation of an external corpus into validated :class:`Document` records.
2	
3	The acquisition pipeline pulls rows in whatever shape the source publishes them
4	(the NOSIBLE Hugging Face datasets use ``text`` / ``label`` / ``netloc`` / ``url``)
5	and this module maps them onto the project's own schema. The field mapping is data,
6	not code, so a second source — the NOSIBLE Search API, a local dump — only needs a
7	new ``field_map`` in ``conf/``, never a new normaliser.
8	
9	Determinism
10	-----------
11	Document ids are derived by hashing the source's natural key, so re-running the
12	pipeline over the same pinned revision yields the same ids, and therefore the same
13	shard assignments and the same byte-for-byte index.
14	
15	Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — the "Documents" node
16	    that opens the build-time half of the architecture diagram, upstream of text
17	    processing and embedding. Local copy:
18	    ``data/00_reference/the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md``.
19	
20	Assumptions:
21	    - A public corpus contains junk. Rows that are empty or shorter than
22	      ``min_text_chars`` are skipped, not raised on, because one malformed row out
23	      of 100,000 must not fail a multi-hour production build.
24	    - The source's ``url`` is a natural key. Where it is absent the body text is
25	      hashed instead, so every row still gets a stable id rather than colliding on
26	      the empty string.
27	    - Passages arrive untitled. A title is derived from the first sentence because
28	      the shard manifest, the shard summary, and the ``title\\ntext`` embedding
29	      input all assume one exists.
30	
31	Alternatives considered:
32	    - A normaliser class per source: the obvious object-oriented shape, and the
33	      right one once sources need genuinely different logic. Rejected while the
34	      difference between sources is only *which column holds what*, which a
35	      declarative ``field_map`` expresses without new code.
36	    - Sequential ids (``doc-000001``): shorter and readable. Rejected because they
37	      depend on row order, so re-fetching a corpus whose rows were reordered would
38	      renumber every document and silently invalidate the stored judgments.
39	    - Raising on unusable rows: better for a small curated corpus where every row is
40	      supposed to be valid. Rejected here for the reason in the assumptions above.
41	"""
42	
43	from __future__ import annotations
44	
45	import hashlib
46	import re
47	from typing import Any
48	
49	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
50	
51	from cybernaut_mini.models import Document
52	
53	#: Cap on a derived title. Long enough to be a useful routing signal, short enough
54	#: that it does not swamp the body text when the two are concatenated for embedding.
55	_TITLE_MAX_CHARS = 120
56	
57	_SENTENCE_END = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+")
58	_WHITESPACE = re.compile(r"\s+")
59	
60	
61	class CorpusSourceConfig(BaseModel):
62	    """How to turn raw source rows into :class:`Document` records."""
63	
64	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
65	
66	    #: Source column -> Document field. Values must name real Document fields.
67	    field_map: dict[str, str] = Field(
68	        default_factory=lambda: {
69	            "text": "text",
70	            "url": "url",
71	        }
72	    )
73	    #: Source columns copied verbatim into ``Document.metadata``.
74	    metadata_fields: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
75	    #: Applied when the source carries no per-row language column.
76	    default_language: str | None = "en"
77	    #: Prefix for generated ids, so documents from different sources cannot collide.
78	    id_prefix: str = "doc"
79	    #: Drop documents whose body is shorter than this (boilerplate, nav text).
80	    min_text_chars: int = Field(default=32, ge=0)
81	
82	
83	class CorpusNormalizeError(ValueError):
84	    """Raised when a source cannot be mapped onto the Document schema at all."""
85	
86	
87	def _clean(value: Any) -> str:
88	    """Collapse whitespace in a source value; non-strings become empty."""
89	    if not isinstance(value, str):
90	        return ""
91	    return _WHITESPACE.sub(" ", value).strip()
92	
93	
94	def derive_title(text: str) -> str:
95	    """Use the first sentence as the title, truncated on a word boundary.
96	
97	    These corpora ship passages without titles, but the shard manifest, the shard
98	    summary, and the ``title\\ntext`` embedding input all assume one exists.
99	    """
100	    first = _SENTENCE_END.split(text, maxsplit=1)[0].strip()
101	    if not first:
102	        first = text.strip()
103	    if len(first) <= _TITLE_MAX_CHARS:
104	        return first
105	    clipped = first[:_TITLE_MAX_CHARS].rsplit(" ", 1)[0].strip()
106	    # A single token longer than the cap leaves nothing after rsplit; hard-cut it.
107	    return clipped or first[:_TITLE_MAX_CHARS]
108	
109	
110	def make_document_id(prefix: str, natural_key: str) -> str:
111	    """Stable id from the row's natural key, so ids survive a re-run."""
112	    digest = hashlib.blake2b(natural_key.encode("utf-8"), digest_size=8).hexdigest()
113	    return f"{prefix}-{digest}"
114	
115	
116	def normalize_rows(
117	    rows: list[dict[str, Any]],
118	    config: CorpusSourceConfig,
119	) -> list[Document]:
120	    """Map raw source rows onto validated, deduplicated :class:`Document` records.
121	
122	    Rows that are unusable — no body text, or shorter than ``min_text_chars`` — are
123	    skipped rather than raised on: a 100k-row public corpus is expected to contain
124	    some junk, and one bad row must not fail a production build. Duplicate natural
125	    keys collapse to their first occurrence. Ordering is by document id so the
126	    result is independent of the source's row order.
127	
128	    Raises :class:`CorpusNormalizeError` only for problems that make the *whole*
129	    source unusable, such as a ``field_map`` that never resolves a text column.
130	    """
131	    if not rows:
132	        return []
133	
134	    text_sources = [src for src, dest in config.field_map.items() if dest == "text"]
135	    if not text_sources:
136	        msg = "field_map must map exactly one source column onto 'text'"
137	        raise CorpusNormalizeError(msg)
138	    text_source = text_sources[0]
139	
140	    available = set(rows[0].keys())
141	    if text_source not in available:
142	        msg = (
143	            f"source column {text_source!r} (mapped to 'text') is absent from the "
144	            f"corpus; available columns: {sorted(available)}"
145	        )
146	        raise CorpusNormalizeError(msg)
147	
148	    documents: dict[str, Document] = {}
149	    for row in rows:
150	        text = _clean(row.get(text_source))
151	        if len(text) < config.min_text_chars:
152	            continue
153	
154	        fields: dict[str, Any] = {}
155	        for source_field, dest_field in config.field_map.items():
156	            if dest_field == "text":
157	                continue
158	            value = _clean(row.get(source_field))
159	            if value:
160	                fields[dest_field] = value
161	
162	        metadata = {
163	            name: row[name] for name in config.metadata_fields if row.get(name) is not None
164	        }
165	
166	        # Prefer the source url as the natural key; fall back to the body so rows
167	        # without one still get a stable id rather than colliding on the empty string.
168	        natural_key = fields.get("url") or text
169	        doc_id = make_document_id(config.id_prefix, str(natural_key))
170	        if doc_id in documents:
171	            continue
172	
173	        documents[doc_id] = Document(
174	            id=doc_id,
175	            title=fields.get("title") or derive_title(text),
176	            text=text,
177	            url=fields.get("url"),
178	            language=fields.get("language") or config.default_language,
179	            published_at=fields.get("published_at"),
180	            metadata=metadata,
181	        )
182	
183	    return [documents[key] for key in sorted(documents)]
184

236	def _build_index_impl(index_path: Path) -> None:
237	    """Build a deterministic hash-embedded index from _CORPUS into index_path."""
238	    from cybernaut_mini.indexing import (
239	        _shard_summary,
240	        _shard_title,
241	        compute_entities,
242	        compute_keywords,
243	        compute_shard_term_graphs,
244	    )
245	
246	    processor = TextProcessor(use_spacy=False)
247	    embedder = HashEmbedder(dim=64)
248	
249	    docs = _CORPUS
250	    texts = [f"{doc.title}\n{doc.text}" for doc in docs]
251	
252	    # Embed.
253	    vectors = embedder.embed_documents(texts)
254	
255	    # Shard.
256	    n_shards = 4
257	    seed = 42
258	    shard_result = shard_documents(vectors, n_shards=n_shards, seed=seed)
259	    labels = shard_result.labels
260	    centroids = shard_result.centroids
261	
262	    # Tokenize.
263	    doc_tokens: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
264	    doc_entities: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
265	    for doc in docs:
266	        combined = f"{doc.title}\n{doc.text}"
267	        doc_tokens[doc.id] = processor.content_tokens(combined)
268	        doc_entities[doc.id] = []  # regex backend returns no entities
269	
270	    # Group by shard.
271	    shard_doc_ids: dict[int, list[str]] = {s: [] for s in range(n_shards)}
272	    for idx, doc in enumerate(docs):
273	        shard_doc_ids[labels[idx]].append(doc.id)
274	
275	    row_map = {doc.id: idx for idx, doc in enumerate(docs)}
276	
277	    shard_tokens: dict[int, list[str]] = {
278	        s: [tok for doc_id in ids for tok in doc_tokens.get(doc_id, [])]
279	        for s, ids in shard_doc_ids.items()
280	    }
281	
282	    keywords_by_shard = compute_keywords(shard_tokens, max_keywords=30)
283	    # One graph per shard, from that shard's own documents — the same call the Kedro
284	    # build node makes. A single graph over the whole corpus (what this fixture used
285	    # to build) gives every manifest an identical, corpus-sized graph, so every test
286	    # that reaches manifest.term_graph would exercise behaviour the shipped build no
287	    # longer produces. write_index emits GlobalTermGraphWarning when it sees one.
288	    term_graph_by_shard = compute_shard_term_graphs(
289	        shard_doc_ids,
290	        doc_tokens,
291	        window=5,
292	        min_edge_count=2,
293	        priority_terms={
294	            shard_id: [kw.term for kw in keywords]
295	            for shard_id, keywords in keywords_by_shard.items()
296	        },
297	    )
298	
299	    embedding_model = f"hash-{embedder.dim}"
300	
301	    manifests: list[ShardManifest] = []
302	    for shard_id in range(n_shards):
303	        doc_ids = shard_doc_ids[shard_id]
304	        centroid = centroids[shard_id]
305	        shard_entity_lists = [doc_entities.get(doc_id, []) for doc_id in doc_ids]
306	        entities = compute_entities(shard_entity_lists, max_entities=30)
307	        keywords = keywords_by_shard[shard_id]
308	        doc_by_id = {doc.id: doc for doc in docs}
309	        summary = _shard_summary(shard_id, doc_ids, doc_by_id, vectors, row_map, centroid)
310	        title = _shard_title(shard_id, keywords)
311	        manifests.append(
312	            ShardManifest(
313	                shard_id=shard_id,
314	                document_ids=doc_ids,
315	                centroid=centroid.tolist(),
316	                title=title,
317	                summary=summary,
318	                keywords=keywords,
319	                entities=entities,
320	                term_graph=term_graph_by_shard[shard_id],
321	                document_count=len(doc_ids),
322	                embedding_model=embedding_model,
323	            )
324	        )
325	
326	    meta = IndexMeta(
327	        embedding_model=embedding_model,
328	        embedding_dim=vectors.shape[1],
329	        n_shards=n_shards,

332	    )

334	    write_index(

3	All JSON-bearing datasets serialize through :func:`cybernaut_mini.models.canonical_dumps`
4	so pipeline outputs keep the byte-for-byte determinism guarantee.

6	Every path the corpus and the index travel goes through a dataset in this module,
7	so the catalog — not a node body — owns all file and network I/O. That is what makes
8	``kedro-viz`` show real lineage and what lets ``conf/prod`` swap a local corpus for a
9	Hugging Face one without touching pipeline code.

25	#: Committed fixture directories. A pipeline writing here would silently rewrite the
26	#: golden corpus that the determinism tests compare against, so saves are refused.
27	#: Reads are unaffected — `--input data/sample/documents.jsonl` stays supported.
28	PROTECTED_DIRS = ("data/sample", "data/00_reference")

31	def _guard_protected(filepath: Path) -> None:
32	    """Refuse to write over a committed fixture."""
33	    try:
34	        relative = filepath.resolve().relative_to(Path.cwd().resolve())
35	    except ValueError:
36	        # Outside the project (e.g. a pytest tmp_path); nothing to protect.
37	        return
38	    as_posix = relative.as_posix()
39	    for protected in PROTECTED_DIRS:
40	        if as_posix == protected or as_posix.startswith(f"{protected}/"):
41	            msg = (
42	                f"refusing to write {as_posix}: {protected} holds committed fixtures. "
43	                f"Point this catalog entry at a generated layer "
44	                f"(data/01_raw, data/02_intermediate, data/03_primary) instead."
45	            )
46	            raise DatasetError(msg)

50	    """A single JSON value written with the canonical writer."""

250

252	    performs the canonical write; ``load`` returns a query-ready
253	    :class:`~cybernaut_mini.indexing.LoadedIndex`. Keeping the conversion here means
254	    nodes stay pure functions over plain data and never touch the filesystem.
255	    """

258	        self._filepath = Path(filepath)
259

261	        from cybernaut_mini.indexing import LoadedIndex
262	
263	        return LoadedIndex.load(self._filepath)
264	
265	    def save(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
266	        from cybernaut_mini.indexing import write_index
267	        from cybernaut_mini.models import Document, IndexMeta, ShardManifest
268	
269	        try:
270	            meta = IndexMeta.model_validate(data["meta"])
271	            documents = [Document.model_validate(d) for d in data["documents"]]
272	            manifests = [ShardManifest.model_validate(m) for m in data["manifests"]]
273	            vectors = np.array(data["vectors"], dtype=np.float32)
274	            doc_tokens: dict[str, list[str]] = data["doc_tokens"]
275	        except KeyError as exc:
276	            msg = f"ShardIndexDataset payload is missing key {exc}"
277	            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc
278	
279	        write_index(
280	            self._filepath,
281	            meta=meta,
282	            documents=documents,
283	            vectors=vectors,
284	            manifests=manifests,
285	            doc_tokens=doc_tokens,
286	        )

class HuggingFaceDataset(AbstractDataset[None, list[dict[str, Any]]]):
    """Read-only corpus source backed by a Hugging Face Hub dataset repo.

    ``revision`` is **required and must be a commit SHA or tag**, never a branch
    name: a production shard is only reproducible if the corpus it was built from
    is pinned. ``main`` is rejected outright.

    Set ``streaming=True`` for large datasets (CC-News is hundreds of GB in full):
    the loader opens an :class:`~datasets.IterableDataset` over Arrow shards and
    uses :func:`itertools.islice` so only ``max_rows`` rows are downloaded rather
    than materialising a whole shard boundary.

    Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — CC-News as a
        corpus source; 200k-document builds are the target scale (Phase 1.2).

    Assumptions: ``IterableDataset.features`` is populated from the dataset's
        Arrow schema metadata without iterating rows, so the missing-column check
        can inspect it before consuming any data. When ``features`` is ``None``
        (a dynamically typed transform was chained upstream), the check falls back
        to the first row's keys and re-inserts that row so nothing is lost.

    Alternatives rejected: using ``IterableDataset.select_columns`` for projection
        in streaming mode. Supported since ``datasets>=2.4`` but adds another lazy
        wrapper; a per-row dict comprehension is simpler and independent of the
        exact ``datasets`` API version.

    Requires the ``hf`` extra (``uv sync --extra hf``). The import is deferred to
    :meth:`load` so the core package — and the whole offline test suite — never
    depends on it.
    """

    #: Refs that move over time and so cannot pin a reproducible build.
    _MUTABLE_REFS = frozenset({"main", "master", "head", "refs/heads/main"})

    #: Shipped in conf/prod as a deliberate tripwire — a real SHA must replace it.
    _PLACEHOLDER_REF = "replace_with_commit_sha"

    def __init__(
        self,
        repo_id: str,
        revision: str,
        split: str = "train",
        columns: list[str] | None = None,
        max_rows: int | None = None,
        token_env: str = "HF_TOKEN",
        streaming: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        normalized_ref = (revision or "").strip().lower()
        if normalized_ref == self._PLACEHOLDER_REF:
            msg = (
                f"HuggingFaceDataset({repo_id!r}): revision is still the placeholder. "
                f"Resolve the real SHA and paste it into conf/prod/catalog.yml:\n"
                f"  uv run python -c \"from huggingface_hub import HfApi; "
                f"print(HfApi().dataset_info('{repo_id}').sha)\""
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg)
        if not normalized_ref or normalized_ref in self._MUTABLE_REFS:
            msg = (
                f"HuggingFaceDataset({repo_id!r}): revision must pin an immutable "
                f"commit SHA or tag, got {revision!r}. A moving ref makes the built "
                f"index unreproducible."
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg)
        self._repo_id = repo_id
        self._revision = revision
        self._split = split
        self._columns = columns
        self._max_rows = max_rows
        self._token_env = token_env
        self._streaming = streaming

    def load(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        try:
            # The Hugging Face `datasets` package, not this module: Python 3 has no
            # implicit relative imports, so the absolute name wins despite the clash.
            from datasets import load_dataset
        except ImportError as exc:
            msg = (
                "HuggingFaceDataset needs the 'hf' extra; install it with "
                "`uv sync --extra hf`"
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc

        # A private repo needs a token; a public one must still work without it.
        token = os.environ.get(self._token_env) or None

        if self._streaming:
            return self._load_streaming(load_dataset, token)
        return self._load_eager(load_dataset, token)

    def _load_eager(self, load_dataset: Any, token: str | None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Non-streaming path: byte-identical to the original implementation."""
        split = self._split
        if self._max_rows is not None:
            # Slice in the split spec so only the requested rows are materialised.
            split = f"{split}[:{self._max_rows}]"

        dataset = load_dataset(
            self._repo_id,
            revision=self._revision,
            split=split,
            token=token,
        )
        if self._columns is not None:
            missing = set(self._columns) - set(dataset.column_names)
            if missing:
                msg = (
                    f"HuggingFaceDataset({self._repo_id!r}): requested columns "
                    f"{sorted(missing)} are absent; available: {sorted(dataset.column_names)}"
                )
                raise DatasetError(msg)
            dataset = dataset.select_columns(self._columns)

        rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = [dict(row) for row in dataset]
        return rows

    def _load_streaming(self, load_dataset: Any, token: str | None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Streaming path: opens an IterableDataset and slices with islice."""
        import itertools

        dataset = load_dataset(
            self._repo_id,
            revision=self._revision,
            split=self._split,
            token=token,
            streaming=True,
        )

        it: Any = iter(dataset)

        if self._columns is not None:
            # Prefer features (populated from Arrow schema, no rows consumed).
            features = getattr(dataset, "features", None)
            if features is not None:
                available = set(features.keys())
            else:
                # Fall back to the first row's keys; re-insert it so nothing is lost.
                try:
                    first_row = next(it)
                except StopIteration:
                    return []
                available = set(first_row.keys())
                it = itertools.chain([first_row], it)

            missing = set(self._columns) - available
            if missing:
                msg = (
                    f"HuggingFaceDataset({self._repo_id!r}): requested columns "
                    f"{sorted(missing)} are absent; available: {sorted(available)}"
                )
                raise DatasetError(msg)

        if self._max_rows is not None:
            it = itertools.islice(it, self._max_rows)

        if self._columns is not None:
            cols = self._columns
            return [{col: row[col] for col in cols} for row in it]
        return [dict(row) for row in it]

    def save(self, data: None) -> None:
        msg = (
            f"HuggingFaceDataset({self._repo_id!r}) is read-only; write the "
            f"normalised corpus to a JsonlDataset in data/01_raw instead."
        )
        raise DatasetError(msg)

    def _exists(self) -> bool:
        # Existence would require a network round-trip; report False so Kedro
        # never treats a Hub lookup as a cheap local check.
        return False

    def _describe(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "repo_id": self._repo_id,
            "revision": self._revision,
            "split": self._split,
            "columns": self._columns,
            "max_rows": self._max_rows,
            "streaming": self._streaming,
        }

class _FakeIterableDataset:
    """Minimal stand-in for datasets.IterableDataset in streaming mode."""

    def __init__(self, rows: list[dict[str, Any]], features: dict[str, Any] | None) -> None:
        self._rows = rows
        # Mirrors IterableDataset.features: a dict-like object or None.
        self.features = features

    def __iter__(self) -> Any:
        return iter(self._rows)


def _install_fake_datasets(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]],
    features: dict[str, Any] | None,
) -> None:

    iterable = _FakeIterableDataset(rows, features)
    fake = types.ModuleType("datasets")
    fake.load_dataset = lambda *a, **kw: iterable  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "datasets", fake)

82	    metadata_equals: dict[str, Any] | None = selection_params.get("metadata_equals")
83	    max_documents: int | None = selection_params.get("max_documents")

90	        if metadata_equals is not None and any(

92	        ):

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# MIRACL qrels → Judgment loader                                      #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

_MIRACL_ID_PREFIX = "mir"


def load_miracl_judgments(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[Judgment]:
    """Map structured MIRACL en-dev rows onto :class:`~cybernaut_mini.models.Judgment` records.

    The catalog entry for ``miracl_en_dev_source`` is backed by
    ``HuggingFaceDataset("miracl/miracl", config="en", split="dev")``, which returns
    rows with four fields: ``query_id`` (str), ``query`` (str), ``positive_passages``
    (list of ``{docid, title, text}`` with relevance grade=1), and
    ``negative_passages`` (list of ``{docid, title, text}`` with relevance grade=0).

    Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — the evaluation
        substrate used to record per-mode recall/nDCG/MRR baselines. Local copy:
        ``data/00_reference/the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md``.

    Assumptions:
        - ``relevant_document_ids`` holds ALL graded docids (both 0 and 1), not only
          the positives. The Judgment model stores ``dict[str, int]`` so both grades
          survive; downstream eval nodes compute nDCG correctly from the full set.
        - Docids are keyed as ``make_document_id("mir", passage["docid"])`` to match
          the ``id_prefix="mir"`` used by the MIRACL corpus ingest branch. A judgment
          whose docids use bare MIRACL strings would never match any Document.id.
        - A query row with zero assessments (empty positive AND negative lists) is
          silently skipped rather than raised on; MIRACL en-dev has none of these, but
          robustness beats a fragile length check.

    Alternatives rejected:
        - Accepting raw TSV bytes (``{query_id}\\t{question}`` + TREC qrel format) as
          two separate function arguments. Rejected because the structured
          ``miracl/miracl`` Hub dataset gives the same information already parsed, so
          separate TSV parsing adds code without adding insight.
        - Including only grade=1 docids. Rejected because nDCG requires the full
          relevance pool to distinguish true negatives (grade=0 but retrieved) from
          un-judged documents.

    Raises :class:`ValueError` when ``rows`` is empty (a configuration error — an
    empty MIRACL source is never valid).
    """
    if not rows:
        msg = "MIRACL source returned zero rows; cannot build judgments from an empty dataset"
        raise ValueError(msg)

    judgments: list[Judgment] = []
    for row in rows:
        query_id = str(row["query_id"])
        question = str(row.get("query", ""))

        relevant: dict[str, int] = {}
        for passage in row.get("positive_passages", []):
            doc_id = make_document_id(_MIRACL_ID_PREFIX, str(passage["docid"]))
            relevant[doc_id] = 1
        for passage in row.get("negative_passages", []):
            doc_id = make_document_id(_MIRACL_ID_PREFIX, str(passage["docid"]))
            relevant[doc_id] = 0

        if not relevant:
            # A query with no assessed passages contributes nothing to evaluation.
            continue

        judgments.append(
            Judgment(
                query_id=query_id,
                question=question,
                relevant_document_ids=relevant,
            )
        )

    return judgments


def validate_judgments_against_corpus(
    judgments: list[Judgment],
    corpus_doc_ids: set[str],
) -> None:
    """Assert every judgment docid exists in the built corpus.

    Raises :class:`ValueError` listing up to 20 missing docids so the operator
    can diagnose which MIRACL passages were dropped by the corpus filter step.

    Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — acceptance
        criterion: "Every docid in miracl_en_dev_judgments.jsonl exists in the
        built index." A judgment over a missing doc silently caps recall.

    Assumptions: the corpus ids are passed as a ``set`` so the ``in`` check is O(1)
        per docid rather than O(n). Building the set once before calling this is the
        caller's responsibility.

    Alternatives rejected: returning the list of missing ids and leaving it to the
        caller to decide whether to raise. Rejected because a missing docid is never
        acceptable — it would silently cap recall — so failing loudly is the only
        correct behaviour.
    """
    missing: list[str] = []
    for judgment in judgments:
        for doc_id in judgment.relevant_document_ids:
            if doc_id not in corpus_doc_ids:
                missing.append(doc_id)

    if missing:
        sample = sorted(missing)[:20]
        msg = (
            f"validate_judgments: {len(missing)} judgment docid(s) absent from corpus "
            f"(first 20): {sample}. "
            f"Ensure the MIRACL corpus branch snapshots all qrels docids before selection."
        )
        raise ValueError(msg)

def build_miracl_judgments(
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]],
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Convert structured MIRACL en-dev rows to serialisable Judgment dicts.

    A Kedro node wrapper around :func:`cybernaut_mini.corpus.load_miracl_judgments`.
    The catalog entry ``miracl_en_dev_source`` supplies the rows; the output is
    written to the ``judgments`` catalog entry for downstream evaluation.
    """
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    return [j.model_dump(mode="json") for j in judgments]


def validate_judgments(
    judgments: list[dict[str, Any]],
    documents: list[dict[str, Any]],
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Assert every judgment docid exists in the corpus; pass judgments through.

    A Kedro node wrapper around
    :func:`cybernaut_mini.corpus.validate_judgments_against_corpus`. Wires the
    corpus pipeline's ``documents`` output to the judgment pipeline so validation
    runs after both branches complete.

def _miracl_row(
    query_id: str,
    question: str,
    positives: list[str],
    negatives: list[str] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build a minimal structured MIRACL row (as load_dataset would return)."""
    return {
        "query_id": query_id,
        "query": question,
        "positive_passages": [{"docid": d, "title": "", "text": ""} for d in positives],
        "negative_passages": [{"docid": d, "title": "", "text": ""} for d in (negatives or [])],
    }


def test_load_miracl_judgments_maps_query_id_and_question() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("42", "What is the speed of light?", ["12#0"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert len(judgments) == 1
    assert judgments[0].query_id == "42"
    assert judgments[0].question == "What is the speed of light?"


def test_load_miracl_judgments_prefixes_docids_with_mir() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"], negatives=["99#1"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    doc_ids = set(judgments[0].relevant_document_ids.keys())
    expected_pos = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")
    expected_neg = make_document_id("mir", "99#1")
    assert expected_pos in doc_ids
    assert expected_neg in doc_ids
    # All ids start with the mir prefix
    assert all(k.startswith("mir-") for k in doc_ids)


def test_load_miracl_judgments_preserves_grades() -> None:
    rows = [_miracl_row("1", "Q?", positives=["12#0"], negatives=["99#1"])]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    pos_id = make_document_id("mir", "12#0")
    neg_id = make_document_id("mir", "99#1")
    assert judgments[0].relevant_document_ids[pos_id] == 1
    assert judgments[0].relevant_document_ids[neg_id] == 0


def test_load_miracl_judgments_skips_rows_with_no_assessments() -> None:
    rows = [
        _miracl_row("1", "has passages", positives=["12#0"]),
        _miracl_row("2", "no passages", positives=[], negatives=[]),
    ]
    judgments = load_miracl_judgments(rows)
    assert len(judgments) == 1
    assert judgments[0].query_id == "1"

class MiraclTsvDataset(AbstractDataset[None, list[dict[str, Any]]]):
    """Read MIRACL topics + qrels from Hugging Face Hub TSV files.

    ``load_dataset("miracl/miracl", ...)`` is blocked by a deprecated loading
    script (``miracl.py``). This dataset reads the underlying TSV files directly
    via :class:`huggingface_hub.HfFileSystem` and reassembles them into the same
    structured row format that ``load_dataset`` would have returned::

        {
            "query_id": str,
            "query": str,
            "positive_passages": [{"docid": str}, ...],   # grade 1
            "negative_passages": [{"docid": str}, ...],   # grade 0
        }

    This shape is exactly what :func:`cybernaut_mini.corpus.load_miracl_judgments`
    expects, so no downstream code changes are needed.

    Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — MIRACL as the
        qrels source for eval; docid stability requires using the same TSV files
        that define the qrel identifiers, not a post-hoc HF conversion.
        Local copy: ``docs/blog-archive/the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md``.

    Assumptions:
        - Topics TSV format: ``{query_id}\\t{question}`` (no header, UTF-8).
        - Qrels TSV format: ``{query_id}\\tQ0\\t{docid}\\t{grade}`` (TREC-style,
          no header). Only grades 0 and 1 appear in MIRACL en-dev.
        - Topics with no matching qrel rows are silently dropped (they carry no
          judgment signal and ``load_miracl_judgments`` would skip them anyway).

    Alternatives rejected:
        - Fixing the ``miracl/miracl`` loading script upstream: out of scope for
          this educational replica.
        - Parsing the dataset via ``HuggingFaceDataset`` with a custom config:
          ``datasets`` refuses to load *any* dataset with a deprecated script.
        - Fetching the topics + qrels as two separate Kedro datasets and merging
          in a node: doubles the catalog boilerplate and adds a merge node just
          to satisfy HF's file layout. Wrapping both files in one dataset class
          keeps the Kedro graph identical to the ``load_dataset`` design.

    Requires the ``hf`` extra (``uv sync --extra hf``).
    """

    _MUTABLE_REFS = frozenset({"main", "master", "head", "refs/heads/main"})
    _PLACEHOLDER_REF = "replace_with_commit_sha"

    def __init__(
        self,
        repo_id: str,
        revision: str,
        language: str,
        split: str = "dev",
        token_env: str = "HF_TOKEN",
    ) -> None:
        normalized_ref = (revision or "").strip().lower()
        if normalized_ref == self._PLACEHOLDER_REF:
            msg = (
                f"MiraclTsvDataset({repo_id!r}): revision is still the placeholder. "
                f"Resolve the real SHA and paste it into conf/prod/catalog.yml:\n"
                f"  uv run python -c \"from huggingface_hub import HfApi; "
                f"print(HfApi().dataset_info('{repo_id}').sha)\""
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg)
        if not normalized_ref or normalized_ref in self._MUTABLE_REFS:
            msg = (
                f"MiraclTsvDataset({repo_id!r}): revision must pin an immutable "
                f"commit SHA or tag, got {revision!r}."
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg)
        self._repo_id = repo_id
        self._revision = revision
        self._language = language
        self._split = split
        self._token_env = token_env

    def load(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        try:
            from huggingface_hub import HfFileSystem
        except ImportError as exc:
            msg = (
                "MiraclTsvDataset needs the 'hf' extra; install it with "
                "`uv sync --extra hf`"
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc

        token = os.environ.get(self._token_env) or None
        fs = HfFileSystem(token=token)

        lang = self._language
        split = self._split
        rev = self._revision
        base = f"datasets/{self._repo_id}@{rev}/miracl-v1.0-{lang}"
        topics_path = f"{base}/topics/topics.miracl-v1.0-{lang}-{split}.tsv"
        qrels_path = f"{base}/qrels/qrels.miracl-v1.0-{lang}-{split}.tsv"

        # --- topics: query_id → question ---
        topics: dict[str, str] = {}
        try:
            with fs.open(topics_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                for line in fh:
                    line = line.rstrip("\n")
                    if not line:
                        continue
                    parts = line.split("\t", 1)
                    if len(parts) == 2:
                        topics[parts[0]] = parts[1]
        except DatasetError:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            msg = (
                f"MiraclTsvDataset({self._repo_id!r}): failed to read topics "
                f"from {topics_path!r}: {exc}"
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc

        # --- qrels: query_id → (positives, negatives) ---
        positives: dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]] = {}
        negatives: dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]] = {}
        try:
            with fs.open(qrels_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                for line in fh:
                    line = line.rstrip("\n")
                    if not line:
                        continue
                    parts = line.split("\t")
                    if len(parts) < 4:
                        continue
                    qid, _q0, docid, grade_str = parts[0], parts[1], parts[2], parts[3]
                    entry = {"docid": docid}
                    if grade_str.strip() == "1":
                        positives.setdefault(qid, []).append(entry)
                    else:
                        negatives.setdefault(qid, []).append(entry)
        except DatasetError:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            msg = (
                f"MiraclTsvDataset({self._repo_id!r}): failed to read qrels "
                f"from {qrels_path!r}: {exc}"
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg) from exc

        # --- assemble rows (only topics that have qrel rows) ---
        rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for qid, question in topics.items():
            pos = positives.get(qid, [])
            neg = negatives.get(qid, [])
            if not pos and not neg:
                continue
            rows.append(
                {
                    "query_id": qid,
                    "query": question,
                    "positive_passages": pos,
                    "negative_passages": neg,
                }
            )
        return rows

    def save(self, data: None) -> None:
        msg = (
            f"MiraclTsvDataset({self._repo_id!r}) is read-only; write the "
            f"normalised judgments to a JsonlDataset in data/02_intermediate instead."
        )
        raise DatasetError(msg)

    def _exists(self) -> bool:
        return False

    def _describe(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "repo_id": self._repo_id,
            "revision": self._revision,
            "language": self._language,
            "split": self._split,
        }

class _FakeFile:
    """Context-manager that iterates over pre-loaded lines."""

    def __init__(self, content: str) -> None:
        self._lines = content.splitlines(keepends=True)

    def __enter__(self) -> Any:
        return iter(self._lines)

    def __exit__(self, *a: Any) -> None:
        pass


def _install_fake_hf_filesystem(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    files: dict[str, str],
) -> None:
    """Patch huggingface_hub so MiraclTsvDataset never hits the network."""

    class _FakeFs:
        def __init__(self, token: Any = None) -> None:
            pass

        def open(self, path: str, mode: str = "r", encoding: str = "utf-8") -> _FakeFile:
            if path not in files:
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"fake fs: {path!r} not found")
            return _FakeFile(files[path])

    fake_hf = types.ModuleType("huggingface_hub")
    fake_hf.HfFileSystem = _FakeFs  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "huggingface_hub", fake_hf)


def _default_files() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {_TOPICS_PATH: _SAMPLE_TOPICS, _QRELS_PATH: _SAMPLE_QRELS}

.PHONY: install install-mac install-prod env accel test lint typecheck check \
	build-sample search-sample eval-sample \
	ingest ingest-prod build-prod eval-pipeline viz pipelines \
	notebooks lab entire doctor

install: env
	uv sync

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Native macOS — the default development environment                  #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

# Apple silicon: Accelerate-linked numpy, torch with the MPS backend, and thread
# counts tuned to performance cores. The devcontainer is still supported (see
# `install`) but is native arm64 *Linux*, which reaches none of those.
install-mac: env
	scripts/setup_mac.sh

# What this machine actually offers: BLAS, SIMD, torch backend, resolved device.
# Run it after install-mac, and any time a build looks slower than it should.
accel:
	uv run python -c "from cybernaut_mini.accel import describe; print(describe().render())"

# Corpus acquisition from the Hub plus real sentence-transformers embeddings.
install-prod: env
	uv sync --extra hf --extra st

env:
	python3 scripts/sync_env.py

# Install the Entire CLI and (re)wire its git + Claude Code hooks. Run after a
# release bumps the hook format, or whenever commits print the "[entire] ... not
# installed" warning. Also runs on devcontainer create.
entire:
	scripts/entire_setup.sh

# Verify the container: node/claude/omc/uv/.venv plus kedro, notebooks, catalog
# and Entire.
doctor:
	scripts/devcontainer_doctor.sh

test:
	uv run pytest

lint:
	uv run ruff check .

typecheck:
	uv run mypy src

check: lint typecheck test

build-sample:
	uv run cybernaut-mini build \
		--input data/sample/documents.jsonl \
		--index artifacts/sample \
		--config configs/tiny.yaml

search-sample:
	uv run cybernaut-mini search \
		--index artifacts/sample \
		--mode hybrid \
		--question "What links gut bacteria to immune response?"

eval-sample:
	uv run cybernaut-mini eval \
		--index artifacts/sample \
		--judgments data/sample/judgments.jsonl

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Kedro pipelines                                                     #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

pipelines:
	uv run kedro registry list

# Acquisition only: raw -> intermediate -> primary. Reads the local source
# declared in conf/base/catalog.yml (data/01_raw/corpus_source.jsonl).
ingest:
	uv run kedro run --pipeline corpus_ingest

# Acquisition from the pinned Hugging Face dataset. Needs `make install-prod`
# and, for gated repos, HF_TOKEN.
ingest-prod:
	uv run kedro run --pipeline corpus_ingest --env prod

# Full production shard: acquire, normalise, select, embed, shard, write.
# Aborts immediately unless embedding.revision is pinned in conf/prod.
build-prod:
	uv run kedro run --pipeline production --env prod

# Evaluation through the catalog; writes data/08_reporting/eval_report.json.
eval-pipeline:
	uv run kedro run --pipeline evaluation --params \
		index_path=artifacts/sample,judgments_path=data/sample/judgments.jsonl,embedding.provider=hash,embedding.dim=256,offline=true

viz:
	uv run kedro viz

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# Notebooks                                                           #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

# Execute every notebook headlessly against the real catalog. Also run as part of
# `make check`, so a notebook cannot silently drift off the pipeline.
notebooks:
	uv run pytest tests/test_notebooks.py -q

# JupyterLab with catalog/context/session/pipelines pre-injected (port 8888).
lab:
	scripts/lab.sh

1	"""Kedro session bootstrap for notebooks.
2	
3	``kedro jupyter lab`` injects ``catalog``, ``context``, ``session`` and ``pipelines``
4	into the kernel automatically. Nothing else does — not ``jupyter lab``, not VS Code's
5	notebook editor, and not the headless executor the test suite uses. A notebook that
6	relied on those injected names would therefore only run one way, and would silently
7	stop being verifiable.
8	
9	This module gives notebooks one entry point that works everywhere, so the same file a
10	reader opens in JupyterLab is the file pytest executes.
11	
12	Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — supports the notebooks
13	    that make the build-time claims (shard coherence, uniformity, hybrid fusion)
14	    measurable. Local copy: ``data/00_reference/the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md``.
15	
16	Assumptions:
17	    - Catalog paths are relative to the project root, so the helpers chdir there.
18	      A notebook opened from ``notebooks/`` would otherwise resolve
19	      ``data/sample/documents.jsonl`` against the wrong directory.
20	    - Building the sample index is cheap (hash embedder, 63 documents, well under a
21	      second), so a notebook may build it on demand rather than requiring the reader
22	      to have run ``make build-sample`` first.
23	    - Rebuilding is avoided when ``_VALID`` is present, so a notebook run never
24	      clobbers an index the reader built with different settings.
25	
26	Alternatives considered:
27	    - Requiring ``kedro jupyter lab``: the officially blessed path, and the reason
28	      ``scripts/lab.sh`` exists. Rejected as the *only* path because it cannot be
29	      driven headlessly, so notebooks could not be executed in the test suite — which
30	      is the mechanism that stops them drifting from the pipeline.
31	    - ``%load_ext kedro.ipython`` in each notebook: the standard magic, and it does
32	      work under plain Jupyter. Rejected because it still assumes an IPython kernel
33	      with the extension importable and the cwd already correct, and it returns
34	      nothing a plain ``python -c`` could use.
35	    - A conftest fixture injecting the catalog into the kernel: keeps notebooks
36	      free of bootstrap code. Rejected because the notebook would then be unrunnable
37	      by a human opening it, which defeats the point of shipping notebooks.
38	"""
39	
40	from __future__ import annotations
41	
42	import os
43	from pathlib import Path
44	from typing import Any
45	
46	_MARKER = "pyproject.toml"
47	_bootstrapped = False
48	
49	
50	def project_root(start: Path | None = None) -> Path:
51	    """Walk up from ``start`` to the directory holding the Kedro ``pyproject.toml``."""
52	    current = (start or Path.cwd()).resolve()
53	    for candidate in (current, *current.parents):
54	        marker = candidate / _MARKER
55	        if marker.is_file() and "[tool.kedro]" in marker.read_text(encoding="utf-8"):
56	            return candidate
57	    msg = f"no Kedro project root found above {current}"
58	    raise RuntimeError(msg)
59	
60	
61	def _bootstrap() -> Path:
62	    """Make the project importable to Kedro and chdir to its root (idempotent)."""
63	    global _bootstrapped
64	
65	    root = project_root()
66	    if os.getcwd() != str(root):
67	        os.chdir(root)
68	    if not _bootstrapped:
69	        from kedro.framework.startup import bootstrap_project
70	
71	        bootstrap_project(root)
72	        _bootstrapped = True
73	    return root
74	
75	
76	def kedro_session(env: str = "local", **runtime_params: Any) -> Any:
77	    """Return a fresh :class:`KedroSession` for the project.
78	
79	    ``runtime_params`` are the same values the Typer CLI forwards, so a notebook can
80	    point the catalog at a different corpus or index exactly as ``--input`` does.
81	    """
82	    from kedro.framework.session import KedroSession
83	
84	    root = _bootstrap()
85	    return KedroSession.create(
86	        project_path=root,
87	        env=env,
88	        runtime_params=runtime_params or None,
89	    )
90	
91	
92	def kedro_catalog(env: str = "local", **runtime_params: Any) -> Any:
93	    """Return the Kedro ``DataCatalog`` — the notebook's only data entry point.
94	
95	    Every notebook loads through this rather than opening paths, so a renamed or
96	    repointed dataset surfaces as a failure in the notebook run instead of a
97	    notebook that quietly reads a stale file.
98	    """
99	    with kedro_session(env, **runtime_params) as session:
100	        return session.load_context().catalog
101	
102	
103	def run_pipeline(name: str, env: str = "local", **runtime_params: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
104	    """Run a registered pipeline from a notebook and return its free outputs."""
105	    with kedro_session(env, **runtime_params) as session:
106	        result: dict[str, Any] = session.run(pipeline_name=name)
107	        return result
108	
109	
110	#: Settings that reproduce ``make build-sample`` (configs/tiny.yaml): the hash
111	#: embedder, so a notebook never needs a model download or network access.
112	SAMPLE_BUILD_PARAMS: dict[str, Any] = {
113	    "input_path": "data/sample/documents.jsonl",
114	    "index_path": "artifacts/sample",
115	    "judgments_path": "data/sample/judgments.jsonl",
116	    "embedding": {"provider": "hash", "dim": 256},
117	    "index": {
118	        "n_shards": 8,
119	        "max_keywords": 30,
120	        "max_entities": 30,
121	        "cooccurrence_window": 5,
122	        "min_edge_count": 2,
123	    },
124	    "seed": 42,
125	    "offline": True,
126	}
127	
128	
129	def ensure_sample_index(index_path: str = "artifacts/sample") -> Path:
130	    """Build the sample index if it is absent, then return its path.
131	
132	    ``_VALID`` is written last by the index writer, so its presence means a complete
133	    index and the build is skipped. That keeps a notebook run from overwriting an
134	    index the reader built themselves.
135	    """
136	    root = _bootstrap()
137	    target = root / index_path
138	    if (target / "_VALID").exists():
139	        return target
